title: [NEXT-730] ESLint `no-head-element` rule being checked inside the `app` directory when file path includes `pages/`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

labels.name: linear: next
labels.description: Confirmed issue that is tracked by the Next.js team.

body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```
Operating System:
      Platform: darwin
      Arch: x64
      Version: Darwin Kernel Version 21.6.0: Mon Aug 22 20:17:10 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.140.49~2/RELEASE_X86_64
    Binaries:
      Node: 16.13.1
      npm: 9.4.0
      Yarn: N/A
      pnpm: 7.27.0
    Relevant packages:
      next: 13.2.2-canary.3
      eslint-config-next: 13.2.2-canary.3
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0
```

### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

ESLint (eslint-config-next)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/kfirfitousi/eslint-next-bug

### To Reproduce

1. run `create-next-app` in a directory that includes `pages/` (e.g `/Users/foo/pages/projects/`) and enable `appDir`
2. go to `app/layout.tsx` and add a `<head />` element inside `<html>`
3. run `next lint`


### Describe the Bug

The rule is getting checked inside the `app` directory when the file path includes `pages/`.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37262772/221898215-05e295e2-566d-411a-8fa0-6943d73c1787.png)

### Expected Behavior

The rule should not be checked inside the `app` directory
